key_insight: In the fixed-parameter, expanding-depth QAOA regime, much of the optimization benefit appears to persist even when entanglement is aggressively removed, enabling a near-classical solver.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a low-memory, scalable route to MaxCut-style optimization on large graphs, with practical performance competitive with strong benchmark values without per-instance training.
method: Trained a compact 2-parameter QAOA schedule on small instances and reused it at larger sizes and depths.
Used approximate matrix product state simulations up to 50 qubits and 100 layers to track entanglement via bond dimension.
Introduced BOND-1 by projecting the state to a product state after every two-qubit interaction, yielding a classical QUBO solver.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports BOND-1 achieving cut ratios above 0.95 versus best-known values on GSet MaxCut benchmarks up to 20,000 variables, sometimes matching them, with linear memory cost.
watch_item: The result is regime-specific: it applies to the fixed-parameter expanding-depth setting and should not be taken as evidence that entanglement is unimportant for quantum optimization in general.
paper_title: Disentangling QAOA: From Weakly Entangled Circuits to a Classical QUBO Solver
